GPT-4 (2026) was announced on **June 29, 2026**, retiring alongside the GPT-5 (Instant and Thinking) announcements on **May 28, 2026**. It represents the first major generation after GPT-3.5, offering improved health intelligence, better safety, and newer capabilities across various domains.

Here are some notable updates:

**Key Highlights:**

| Feature | Version | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Safety & Health Intelligence | GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 Mini, and OpenAI o4-mini | Introduced new health intelligence improvements, including warnings, symptom recognition, and risk detection |
| Language Understanding | GPT-4.5 (replaced ChatGPT) | GPT-4.5 replaced ChatGPT and was announced on **February 13, 2026**; it is currently available as part of the OpenAI Partner Network |
| Multi-Modal Capabilities | GPT-4.5 (replaced ChatGPT) | GPT-4.5 introduced support for images, audio, and video input, though it is still based on the same foundational architecture |
| Performance & Speed | GPT-4.5 (replaced ChatGPT) | GPT-4.5 runs faster than prior versions while retaining similar quality |

**Important Context:** GPT-4.5 was originally designed as an endpoint instead of an API service — it ran entirely within the OpenAI platform, meaning developers could still interact with it using their existing ChatGPT APIs. GPT-4 itself became a new product in June 2026, replacing all prior GPT versions (including GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 Mini, and OpenAI o4-mini).

For enterprise customers, the transition from GPT-4o/GPT-4.1 to GPT-4.5 marked a significant shift, with the latter serving as both a product and a service. GPT-4.5 also expanded health intelligence beyond just symptoms recognition to include warnings and disease prediction.

If you're comfortable with Scikit-Learn, move to **PyTorch** — it's great for building deep neural networks (DNNs), which is where many people who learn ML end up using after Scikit. A few people combine elements of these approaches: use Scikit-Learn for the core logic and PyTorch for the actual network implementation, then deploy using Flask or similar. This balances practicality with depth.
